title: codegen/age: write path — :exec methods and write-param coverage
description:
The :exec cardinality for AGE: CREATE/SET/DELETE query emission through the same server-side param mechanism, zero-column cypher() invocation shape (AGE still requires an AS projection clause — the spike corpus documents the zero/one-column form), and command execution over DBTX.Exec. Completes param-encoding coverage for every property type the scalar stage admits, on the write side.

TDD: red goldens first; the live battery's mixed read-write scenarios (write via :exec, re-read via :one/:many, delete, confirm ErrNoRows) enabled for the AGE arm — these already exist backend-invariantly from the live-refactor bead.
acceptance_criteria: Write-path fixtures enrolled for AGE pass golden + compile gates; mixed read-write live scenarios green on the AGE arm; :exec on a projection-shaped query still rejected by shared admission (existing invalid fixtures run under the AGE target).
notes:
MANAGER NOTE AT START (2026-08-01).

Branch feat/codegen-age-write-path, worktree gqlc-35yu10-write, cut from
cdd09ca (post-.9).

Correction to this bead's own description before anyone acts on it: it says
"the spike corpus documents the zero/one-column form". It does not. I read
gqlc-35yu.5 end to end — it captures the temporal encoding table with ordering
evidence, the param mechanism with server-log proof of server-side binding, and
the agtype result-text corpus for reads. Every cypher() invocation recorded
there projects at least one column from a RETURN. There is no CREATE, SET or
DELETE anywhere in it, and so no evidence for what the AS clause must look like
when the Cypher body returns nothing.

So the write invocation shape is NOT settled by prior work and must not be
assumed from the AGE docs alone. Establish it live against the pinned image
first (apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8... — PostgreSQL 18.1, AGE 1.7.0), record the
exact statement and observed output in this bead the way .5 did, and only then
emit against it. The specific things unproven: the column-definition list AGE
demands for a RETURN-less body, whether a write body may project columns at
all, and what pgconn.CommandTag carries back for a cypher() call (AGE's write
happens inside a set-returning function, so the tag is the SELECT's, not the
CREATE's — if RowsAffected is meaningless the emitted :exec must not pretend
otherwise).

Two drop reasons in internal/codegen/age/errors.go unservedReason() are what
this bead removes: "writes to the graph" (Validated.Statement ==
resolver.StatementWrite) and ":exec returns no rows to decode"
(CardinalityExec). They are separate axes and they come off separately — a
:many that writes and returns rows is a different shape from a :exec that
writes and returns none. Whichever this bead does not serve must keep its drop
reason and keep its invalid fixture.

STANDING CONSTRAINTS, unchanged: string interpolation of user args is banned
unconditionally — only the graph name may be interpolated, escaped and
length-checked; everything else binds. No AI attribution in any commit or PR.

LIVE EVIDENCE (2026-08-01), apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8... — AGE 1.7.0 on
PostgreSQL 18.1. Probes were scratch (psql scripts + two pgx v5 programs);
nothing shipped. The three unproven questions, answered.

(1) The column-definition list for a RETURN-less body must be EXACTLY ONE
ag_catalog.agtype column.

  no AS clause:
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher('writeprobe', $$ CREATE (:P {n:1}) $$);
    ERROR:  a column definition list is required for functions returning "record"
  AS () :
    ... $$) AS ();
    ERROR:  syntax error at or near ")"          -- zero columns is not expressible
  two agtype columns:
    ... $$) AS (v0 ag_catalog.agtype, v1 ag_catalog.agtype);
    ERROR:  column definition list for CREATE clause must contain a single
            agtype attribute  (SQLSTATE 42804)
    HINT:   ... cypher($ ... CREATE ... $) AS t(c agtype) ...
  one non-agtype column:  same 42804.
  one agtype column: OK, zero rows returned.

  The same 42804 (text unchanged, still saying "CREATE clause") is what a
  RETURN-less DELETE and a RETURN-less SET give for a two-column list. So the
  emitted shape is "v0 ag_catalog.agtype" whatever the write clause is.

(2) A write body MAY project, and then the list must match the RETURN arity
exactly; a mismatch either way is
    ERROR:  return row and column definition list do not match
  Verified for CREATE ... RETURN p / RETURN p.n, SET ... RETURN p / RETURN
  p.name, MERGE ... RETURN r, DETACH DELETE ... RETURN 1. The existing
  recordShape (one v<i> per RowField) was therefore already correct for
  write-with-projection; only the zero-RowFields case was new.

(3) pgconn.CommandTag is the enclosing SELECT's, not the write's. Measured
through pgx v5.10.0 Conn.Exec:

    CREATE 1 vertex,  bound params      -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    CREATE 3 vertices in one statement  -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    DELETE 2 vertices                   -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    SET on 2 vertices                   -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    DELETE matching nothing             -> "SELECT 0"  RowsAffected=0
    CREATE (p:P {n:5}) RETURN p.n       -> "SELECT 1"  RowsAffected=1
    MATCH (p:P) RETURN p.n  (3 rows)    -> "SELECT 3"  RowsAffected=3

  RowsAffected is the projected row count and nothing else. It cannot tell
  "created three vertices" from "matched nothing". DECISION: the emitted :exec
  returns error alone and discards the tag. Justified twice over — the
  measurement above, and TestBackendInvariantSurface, since the neo4j targets
  emit Method(ctx, ...) error for :exec. A RowsAffected in the AGE signature
  would have broken the surface invariant AND lied.

OTHER LIVE FINDINGS

- All four non-interpolating pgx QueryExecModes (CacheStatement,
  CacheDescribe, DescribeExec, Exec) work on writes. SimpleProtocol — the one
  interpolating mode — fails closed on the write path:
    ERROR:  third argument of cypher function must be a parameter (SQLSTATE 22023)
  Note for the next reader: a QueryExecMode must be passed as the FIRST query
  argument to pgx, not the last; passing it last gives a misleading
  "mismatched param and argument count" (pgx v5 conn.go:41).
- An injection payload bound as a write value is stored as data. Payload
  {"name": "a$gqlc$, $1) AS (v0 ag_catalog.agtype); DROP TABLE canary; --"}
  round-tripped intact and the canary table survived.
- A pgx Query of a RETURN-less write whose rows are never drained still applies
  the write.
- An inline property map matched against a JSON-null parameter matches nothing;
  AGE drops null properties at write time, so no stored vertex carries one.
- MERGE (p:Person {id:9})-[r:AUTHORED|LIKES]->(q:Person {id:10}) RETURN r
    ERROR:  syntax error at or near "|"
  Independently confirms gqlc-35yu.14: AGE 1.7.0 has no relationship-type
  alternation. edge_union_write_projection is still enrolled for AGE (its
  sibling edge-union READ fixtures already are, and the golden/compile gates
  hold the emission); .14 remains the open P1 for the missing live coverage.

CORRECTION TO THE MANAGER NOTE ABOVE. The claim "There is no CREATE, SET or
DELETE anywhere in it" about the gqlc-35yu.5 spike is false. Section C9 of that
spike says verbatim: "Write without RETURN -> ZERO ROWS, but the AS(...) list
still needs exactly one agtype column, e.g. AS (v ag_catalog.agtype)." The
corpus-graph setup in Q3 is a RETURN-less CREATE ... $) AS (v agtype); C8(c)
holds CREATE (n:NullProp {a:1, b:null}) RETURN n and MATCH (n:NullProp) SET
n.a = null RETURN n; C10 holds a RETURN-less CREATE (x:A:B {n:1}). The spike's
C9 answer agrees exactly with what was re-measured here. The manager was right
about the second half though: the probe evidence for the projection question
and for CommandTag genuinely was absent, and CommandTag is the one that changed
a design decision, so the live work was necessary regardless.

DESIGN FORKS TAKEN

- :exec returns error, tag discarded. See (3).
- One statement composition path for reads and writes (writeStatement), so the
  graph name stays the only interpolated thing and it stays inside the escaped,
  length-checked cypherStmt. Writes bind through $1 exactly as reads do.
- write_exec_temporal_param deliberately NOT enrolled for AGE: the type table
  has no TIMESTAMP carrier, so it stays with gqlc-35yu.11.
- Two unit tests had used "a write" as their stand-in for an unserved query
  (TestUnservedQueriesOutrankUnrepresentableWidths in the age package, plus the
  CLI-surface tests TestRunApacheAgeRejectionIsASentinel and
  TestGenerateApacheAgeRejectsQueriesItCannotServe). Writes are served now, so
  each moved to a list-projecting query, which is the narrowest axis AGE still
  refuses. The CLI ones needed a schema of their own: a LIST on the shared
  fixtureSchema would fail the AGE arm of the driver-vocabulary sweep on the
  width sweep instead.

GATES: just test / just lint / just test-codegen-fence / just actionlint /
just test-codegen-live all green. The AGE arm now runs
mixed_read_write_batch: exec + re-read live (arms table flipped writes: true,
which TestLiveSmoke asserts against the harness type, so the arm cannot
silently drop the write scenarios).

MANAGER CORRECTION (2026-08-01), same day, before review.

My start-of-bead note above is WRONG on its central claim and I am leaving it
in place rather than editing it, so the record shows what the implementer was
told.

I wrote that gqlc-35yu.5 has "no CREATE, SET or DELETE anywhere in it" and that
"the write invocation shape is NOT settled by prior work". The implementer
checked and it is false. Spike section C9 says verbatim:

    Write without RETURN -> ZERO ROWS, but the AS(...) list still needs exactly
                            one agtype column, e.g. `AS (v ag_catalog.agtype)`.

I have re-read it at gqlc-35yu.5 lines 751-752 and confirmed. C8(c) and C10
also carry RETURN-less writes, and the Q3 corpus setup is one.

Cause: I searched the spike with grep patterns anchored on `cypher(...CREATE`
and on the `AS (` form, and truncated the output with head before reaching
C9 at line 742. I then reported the absence as a finding. Searching for a
thing, not finding it, and concluding it is not there is only valid if the
search was capable of finding it — mine was not, and I did not check that
before writing the claim into a bead where it would be read as established.

What survives from the note, and what the implementer confirmed was genuinely
unproven and worth the live work:

  - Whether a write body may PROJECT columns. It may; the AS list then matches
    the RETURN arity exactly. C9 covers only the RETURN-less case.
  - What pgconn.CommandTag carries. It is the enclosing SELECT's, not the
    write's: CREATE of 3 vertices, DELETE of 2, and a DELETE matching nothing
    all report "SELECT 0". RowsAffected is the projected-row count and nothing
    else. This changed a design decision — the emitted :exec returns error
    alone and discards the tag, which is also what keeps its signature
    identical to the neo4j targets.

So the probing was worth doing on its own merits, and the corrected lesson is
about how I established the premise, not about whether to measure.

MANAGER FINDING, PRE-REVIEW (2026-08-01). BLOCKING. Reproduced myself before
ruling; not taken from anyone's report.

The AGE query body declares locals named stmt, args, rows and err. A query
with exactly ONE parameter emits that parameter under a name taken from the
query text — writeMethodSignature's `case 1:` arm emits
codegen.LowerFirstRune(p.ParamFields[0].Field). The two namespaces are the
same block, so a parameter the author happens to name $stmt collides with the
composed statement.

Reproduced with a two-file fixture, one query, no other content:

    MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name = $stmt RETURN p.name

emits, for apache-age-pgx-v5:

    func (q *Queries) PersonByStmt(ctx context.Context, stmt string) (string, error) {
        stmt, err := q.cypherStmt("$gqlc$", personByStmtQueryText, "v0 ag_catalog.agtype")
        ...
        args, err := agtypeArgs(map[string]any{"stmt": stmt})
        ...
        rows, err := q.db.Query(ctx, stmt, args)

The caller's argument is overwritten by the composed SQL on the line after it
arrives, and the SQL text is then bound as the value of $stmt. The caller's
value is never read. PersonByStmt(ctx, "Alice") searches for a Person whose
name is the entire generated SQL statement.

THIS COMPILES. `go test ./internal/codegen/conformance/ -update` reports ok,

The verdict is structural rather than a name comparison:
requireNothingDeclaredIsCaptured asserts that every package-level name
the emitted file declares is a free identifier of some method. Capture
has exactly one signature -- the declaration stays, the body still spells
the name, and the name now resolves to the parameter, leaving the
declaration referenced by nobody. Asserting reachability never has to
know what the emitter chose to call anything, which is what makes the set
closed rather than enumerated: a package-level name added later is held
by the same assertion.

agtypeString and decode<Entity> arrive from an import or another file of
the package, so they are not package-level declarations OF THIS FILE and
the assertion does not fire on them; capturing one is a compile failure
of the generated package anyway. ctx and q are signature binders, so they
never enter the free set. That is gqlc-ni66's territory, and the
asymmetry is real: the query-text const is the only silent one, because

description:
Entity-typed columns for the AGE backend: decode agtype vertex/edge composite text (id/label/properties per the spike corpus, including the ::vertex / ::edge suffixes) into the SAME entity structs phase Z names for every backend — the Go surface is backend-invariant; only the decode source differs. Emitted decode helpers live in models.go beside the scalar ones.

The implementer disclosed this himself as "a real regression and it is

DEFECT: an undirected edge pattern whose endpoints share a label makes the resolver
append the SAME schema.EdgeKey twice, because edgeCandidates (internal/resolver/
resolve.go:477) tries both orientations and for src==tgt both orientations are one key.
The round-4 gate reads that repeat as two indistinguishable candidates and refuses.

My repro, schema with two self-loop edge types under DISTINCT labels:
    DIRECTED EDGE TYPE Likes (:Person) -[:LIKES]-> (:Person),
    DIRECTED EDGE TYPE Wrote (:Person) -[:WROTE]-> (:Person)
    MATCH (x:Person)-[r:LIKES|WROTE]-(y:Person) RETURN r

  branch 95dd0b2, apache-age-pgx-v5 -> REFUSED: "candidates Likes and Likes both carry
      edge label \"LIKES\"". The message names one entity twice and prescribes a remedy
      that cannot be followed: both endpoints are already pinned to :Person.
  master bd29f01, neo4j-go-v5 -> 4 cases emitted, LIKES twice and WROTE twice,
      non-compiling.
  master bd29f01, apache-age-pgx-v5 -> refused as out of scope.

That last line is what makes it blocking rather than pre-existing. On AGE this branch is
what introduces edge-union support, and an undirected self-loop union is mainstream. A
capability that refuses it does not meet this bead's acceptance criterion.

LINUS'S PROPOSED FIX SITE IS WRONG, AND I RULE AGAINST IT. He said to dedupe in
closeEdge and NOT in edgeCandidates, because R3 spec 4.6 case C detects the single-label
undirected self-loop off the pre-dedupe length. He read the verdict table and not the
rationale under it. docs/specs/resolver-stage-r3.md, case C rationale, says verbatim:

  "Person -> FOLLOWS -> Person where the reciprocal ... is also declared: the same key,
   so there is no ambiguity. The genuine double-match case requires distinct
   source/target label sets in the two directions."

The pre-dedupe length IS the bug. The implementation contradicts its own spec, and I
confirmed that on master with a single self-loop edge type:

    DIRECTED EDGE TYPE Likes (:Person) -[:LIKES]-> (:Person)
    MATCH (x:Person)-[r:LIKES]-(y:Person) RETURN r
  master bd29f01 -> ambiguous edge orientation: edge "r" matches both
      Person-[LIKES]->Person, Person-[LIKES]->Person

One key listed twice, from a query the spec says is unambiguous. So deduping in
edgeCandidates is the spec-correct fix and closes three things at once: this spec
violation, the duplicate-case non-compiling emission on neo4j, and the branch's new
over-refusal.

I verified the dedupe does not weaken genuine case C. Both resolver fixtures pinning
ErrAmbiguousEdgeOrientation (test/data/resolver/invalid/ambiguous_edge_orientation*.cypher)
use Person/Post, so the two orientations are two DISTINCT keys, the set stays at size 2
after dedupe, and case C still fires.

SCOPE RULING: in scope and blocking. The branch caused the over-refusal, so it fixes it;
you do not ship a regression you introduced and file a bead for it. The correct fix
happens to be ~10 lines in the resolver and also closes a documented spec violation.

Also blocking: the valid corpus contains ZERO undirected multi-label edge patterns. That
blind spot is why round 3's duplicate-case defect and round 4's over-refusal both reached
review, and it is why golden churn kept measuring zero. A valid fixture for the
undirected self-loop union is required.
MANAGER VERIFICATION OF ROUND 5 (cc9d21e), independent.

The over-refusal is fixed at the root. edgeProbes now dedupes by whole schema.EdgeKey
(membership-only map, never iterated, first-occurrence order); edgeCandidates is that
set filtered by s.Edges; describeTriedEdges reuses edgeProbes rather than rebuilding
the enumeration, so the two can no longer drift. Carmack found a third instance of the
duplication in describeTriedEdges that neither Linus nor I had spotted, and fixed it in
the same seam.

Verified by me:
- My exact repro is now a valid fixture (edge_union_undirected_self_loop, verbatim
  schema and query) and emits a clean two-case switch — LIKES then WROTE, once each —
  under BOTH apache-age-pgx-v5 and neo4j-go-v5.
- Zero existing goldens modified. git diff --name-status 95dd0b2 cc9d21e shows every
  golden path as an addition; the only modified non-source file is
  test/data/resolver/valid/schema.mapping.json, which registers the new fixtures.
- unrepresentable_edge_union_shared_label and its _list companion are still red for the
  right reason (LikesFwd and LikesRev are distinct keys, so the dedupe leaves both and
  the round-4 gate still fires).
- Both ambiguous_edge_orientation fixtures still fail with ErrAmbiguousEdgeOrientation.
- Mutation test, mine: deleting the dedupe fails FIVE independent guards across two
  packages — TestEdgeFailMessagesListEachTriedKeyOnce, TestEdgeUnionKeysAreASet, both
  new resolver valid fixtures, and TestConformanceSuite. The fix is braced.
- Gates on cc9d21e: just test PASS, just lint PASS (0 issues), just test-codegen-fence
  PASS (0 issues), just actionlint PASS.

SPEC EDIT ACCEPTED. I had told him not to edit the spec if the spec was right and the
code wrong. He found that a DIFFERENT passage was itself wrong and said so with the
quote rather than complying quietly, which is what I asked for. R3 section 4.4 claimed
"Duplicate EdgeKeys are impossible by construction — the same (label, orientation) pair
generates the same key exactly once". The postcondition is right and the proof is false:
it counts probes, not the keys they name, and (S,T) and (T,S) are two probes but one key
when S == T. He corrected the false lemma, kept the postcondition, left section 4.6 case
C's rationale untouched, and documented the two new fixtures in the coverage sketch.
That is the correct scope.

ROUND 6: REVIEWER VERDICT PASS at cc9d21e. Merged as PR #670, closing #624.

Review took six rounds (three FAILs). What the FAILs found is worth recording,
because two of the three were not AGE defects at all — the AGE work was the
first thing to walk paths that were already broken.

Round 1 FAIL, decoder-local shadowing. A schema property named err/label/out/
props/raw emitted a redeclaration and `generate` still exited 0, because the
format gate only parses. Fixed structurally: every local an emitted decoder
declares is positional. I verified it by deleting the golden and regenerating
byte-identical, then building an 11-hostile-name fixture the implementer had
not seen. The same defect exists on neo4j (I reproduced it on master bd29f01,
6 compile errors) — deferred as gqlc-ak39, since fixing it churns ~77 neo4j
goldens on an AGE-owned branch.

Round 3 FAIL, duplicate-label edge union emitting a duplicate switch case. I
ruled against the reviewer on placement: he wanted it AGE-local, I put it in
the shared admission phase. Neither backend can represent it — an edge value
carries its label and its properties, never its endpoint types — and churn is
zero either way. Reproduction detail worth keeping: the ANONYMOUS edge form was
already refused by Phase Z; only the named DIRECTED EDGE TYPE form got through.

Round 4 FAIL, the gate I ordered OVER-REFUSED. Two self-loop edge types under
DISTINCT labels, queried undirected, were refused as sharing a label — naming
one entity twice and prescribing an unfollowable remedy. The reviewer proposed
a fix site and I found it backwards: he said do not dedupe the enumeration
because R3 §4.6 detects ambiguity off the pre-dedupe length. But §4.6's own
rationale (case C) says the same key in both orientations is unambiguous, so
the pre-dedupe length IS the bug and §4.4's lemma asserting duplicates are
impossible was simply false. Confirmed independently on master: a single
self-loop edge type already gave `ambiguous edge orientation: edge "r" matches
both Person-[LIKES]->Person, Person-[LIKES]->Person`. Fixed by deduping in the
enumeration; §4.4's lemma corrected rather than worked around.

The implementer then found a third instance himself — describeTriedEdges
rebuilt the same enumeration for ErrUnknownEdge's message and repeated keys for
the same reason. Both now read one enumeration.

Independent verification at cc9d21e before authorizing merge: zero MODIFIED
goldens (git diff --name-status 95dd0b2..cc9d21e — every golden path is A);
the new fixture emits one case per declared type on both targets; both
unrepresentable_edge_union fixtures still red with the right sentinel; both
ambiguous_edge_orientation fixtures still red. Mutation test: deleting the
dedupe fails FIVE guards across two packages. Five gates green including
`sg docker -c 'just test-codegen-live'`.

Non-blocking items from round 6 filed as gqlc-kph4 (P2 — the plural-endpoint ×
undirected edge-closure path has zero corpus coverage, and round 5 changes
behaviour there) and gqlc-monh (P3 — rationale text incomplete or reaching
across layers at three sites).

Method note for later beads: the reviewer's PASS was accepted only after
reading his actual verdict and re-running the evidence. Twice in this bead the
reviewer's diagnosis was right and his prescribed fix was wrong. A FAIL is
information about where to look, not an instruction.
close_reason: Merged as cdd09ca (PR #670), closing #624. Reviewer PASS at cc9d21e after six rounds.

title: codegen/age: live adapter arm + nightly CI wiring
description:
Bring the AGE arm into the shared live scenario battery: adapter implementing the per-backend harness interface — apache/age container image pinned by digest, not tag (gqlc-9u5 precedent: tag drift can serve a stale cached PASS from the Go test cache); pgx pool constructed with SessionInit as AfterConnect; seed(cypher) via ag_catalog.cypher over the pool; isolation = unique graph per scenario via EnsureGraph + Cleanup DropGraph, so AGE sub-tests run in parallel (unlike the serialized neo4j DETACH-wipe arms) and the lifecycle helpers get exercised as the isolation mechanism itself.

CI: the arm joins the existing codegen_live nightly/manual job. PR CI wall-time must be untouched — the codegen_live tag boundary already guarantees that; do not add the arm to any PR-triggered workflow. GQLC_SKIP_LIVE behavior extends to the AGE arm. Watch the second nightly run for cache steady-state if any actions/cache path changes (bd memory: first run after a path change is cold).
acceptance_criteria: Shared battery (scalar scenarios) green against a live AGE container locally under -tags codegen_live; nightly job runs the AGE arm and fails red on a seeded assertion break (prove the gate fails, not just that a check exists); AGE sub-tests demonstrably parallel (unique graph names in logs); PR CI workflow diff shows no new PR-time steps; SessionInit FAILURE path covered — a pool whose sessions lack ag_catalog on search_path must fail at pool ACQUISITION, with the test proving the canary discriminates (a canary literal that survives agtype_to_bool would pass on the broken session and must be shown not to be the one shipped).
notes:
SCHEDULING: gqlc-3eyw (codegen_live code is outside every lint gate) is deliberately NOT a blocking dependency of this bead — .8 can ship unlinted exactly as .4 did, and a hard edge would stall the epic critical path on a config decision. But .8 widens the unlinted surface with the AGE adapter arm, so settle gqlc-3eyw BEFORE starting .8 if the slot is free. It is small config work.
=== SessionInit FAILURE-PATH REQUIREMENT, INHERITED FROM .6 (recorded 2026-08-01) ===
.6's notes carry: "Test the failure path, not just the happy path: a connection
whose search_path lacks ag_catalog must be REJECTED by SessionInit, and that
rejection must be observable as a pool-acquisition failure."

.6 is a golden-EMISSION bead — it has no live container and no pool, so that
requirement is not dischargeable there and .6 will not be held for it. It lands
here, where the pool and the container both exist for the first time. Recorded
now so the deferral survives outside a commit message.

WHY IT IS SHARP, NOT CEREMONIAL: the canary's discriminating power depends on
the literal chosen. The .6 review established that
  SELECT '1'::ag_catalog.agtype = '1'::ag_catalog.agtype
fails on a misconfigured session inside agtype_to_bool — i.e. for a reason
unrelated to operator resolution via search_path. A canary using a literal that
happens to survive agtype_to_bool (e.g. 'true') would PASS on a connection with
ag_catalog off the path, which is exactly the deployment the canary exists to
reject. So the failure path is what proves the canary is the right canary; the
happy path proves nothing.

HOW TO APPLY: add a scenario that builds a pool whose AfterConnect runs
SessionInit against a session with ag_catalog deliberately off search_path, and
assert pool acquisition FAILS. Assert on the rejection being observable at
acquire time, not merely that some error exists somewhere.
=== NON-SUPERUSER ARM REQUIREMENT, INHERITED FROM .6 (recorded 2026-08-01) ===
The harness MUST exercise at least one arm connecting as a NON-SUPERUSER role,
not only as postgres.

WHY: .6 round 2 shipped a SessionInit whose first statement was LOAD 'age'. I
verified against the pinned image that LOAD 'age' is superuser-only:

  LOAD 'age' as postgres  -> LOAD, rc=0
  LOAD 'age' as appuser   -> ERROR: access to library "age" is not allowed

Because an error returned from pgxpool's AfterConnect DISCARDS the connection,
that statement bricked the entire pool for any least-privilege role: the pool
would never yield a usable connection at all. A total, deployment-fatal defect.

And it would have sailed straight through this bead's battery, because the
harness connects as postgres. A green live suite would have certified it. The
bug was caught by adversarial review, not by the tests that exist to catch
exactly this class of thing. That is the gap this requirement closes.

HOW TO APPLY: create a role with only the privileges a generated client
actually needs (no SUPERUSER), and run the scalar battery — or at minimum the
pool-construction and one read scenario — as that role. Treat "works as
postgres" as proving nothing about deployability. Any future statement added to
SessionInit is then privilege-checked by construction rather than by review.

Related: LOAD 'age' is now DELETED from SessionInit (see gqlc-35yu.6 notes).
The canary is the loader -- its '+' is an AGE C function, so evaluating it
forces the implicit library load and _PG_init before any user query is parsed.
=== TWO RECORDED FACTS ON THIS BEAD ARE WRONG (verified 2026-08-01) ===

(1) "PR CI wall-time must be untouched -- the codegen_live tag boundary
already guarantees that". FALSE. .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml carried
`on: pull_request` and its own header called it a "PR-blocking merge gate"
(bd gqlc-rvw promoted it). The tag boundary keeps codegen_live out of the
DEFAULT build; it does not keep it out of PR CI, because that workflow passes
the tag explicitly. Adding the AGE arm to `just test-codegen-live` would have
added an apache/age container boot to every pull request.

RESOLUTION: the battery is now split by backend at the recipe level and the
workflow runs one job per backend.
  test-codegen-live        everything (local + as the union)
  test-codegen-live-neo4j  -run TestLiveSmoke -skip TestLiveSmoke/apache-age
  test-codegen-live-age    -run 'TestLiveSmoke|TestAGESessionInit'
                           -skip TestLiveSmoke/neo4j
Job `neo4j` keeps every existing trigger; job `apache-age` carries
`if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`. -skip rather than a narrower -run
so an arm named in neither half shows up as skipped instead of silently
vanishing. Verified empirically that -skip does not run the excluded
subtest body: the neo4j half boots only neo4j (18.3s, unchanged), the AGE
half boots only apache/age.

(2) HOW TO APPLY for the SessionInit failure path -- "build a pool whose
AfterConnect runs SessionInit against a session with ag_catalog deliberately
off search_path" -- is NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE. SessionInit's own first statement
unconditionally prepends ag_catalog to the search_path, so no session it runs
on can be off the path by the time the canary executes. Worse, every failure
reachable that way (extension absent, role lacks USAGE) fails the shipped
canary and a weak canary IDENTICALLY, so it does not demonstrate
discrimination at all.

RESOLUTION: decomposed into three separately provable properties, all in
TestAGESessionInit (test/data/codegen/live_age_session_test.go):

  (A) acquisition-time refusal on genuinely broken deployments. Table over
      a role with no USAGE on ag_catalog (SQLSTATE 42501) and a database with
      no age extension (3F000). Each asserts: a plain pgx.Connect on the same
      DSN SUCCEEDS (so it is the session being refused, not the credentials);
      pgxpool.NewWithConfig succeeds; Acquire fails wrapped in "gqlc: AGE
      operator canary"; pool.Stat().TotalConns() == 0.

  (B) acquire-observable A/B, which is the discrimination proof. A database
      with age installed, granted and on the path, from which only
      ag_catalog.+(agtype,agtype) has been removed (ALTER EXTENSION age DROP
      OPERATOR, then DROP OPERATOR). A pool running a hook whose probe is
      'true'::agtype = 'true'::agtype ACQUIRES; a pool running the shipped
      SessionInit FAILS to acquire with 42883. The two hooks share the
      shipped hook's own search_path statement, captured from it via a
      pgx.QueryTracer, so the probe is the only thing they differ in.

  (C) statement replay on a real off-search_path session, with the canary
      taken from the tracer capture rather than retyped. Rejected-literal
      table:
        shipped '1'+'1' = '2'  -> 42883 (operator resolution)
        'true' = 'true'        -> succeeds, returns true (would false-pass)
        '1' = '1'              -> 22023, cannot cast agtype integer to
                                  type boolean, i.e. fails for an unrelated
                                  reason
      NOTE: .6's note names the '1' = '1' failure as being "inside
      agtype_to_bool". Confirmed exactly: cannot_cast_agtype_value,
      agtype.c:2744. Its SQLSTATE is 22023, not 42846.

  (D) a fence that every AGE target's emitted SessionInit issues byte-identical
      statements, which is what licenses one pool serving handles generated
      into several packages.
=== NON-SUPERUSER ARM: MINIMUM GRANT SET, EMPIRICALLY DERIVED ===

.6's note implies a bare `appuser` could run the canary. It cannot. A plain
LOGIN role with no grants gets, on the shipped canary:
  ERROR: 42501: permission denied for schema ag_catalog
AGE grants nothing to PUBLIC. The minimum set a generated client needs is
three grants, one per emitted requirement (ageAppGrants in live_age_test.go):
  GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA ag_catalog          every emitted statement names it
  GRANT SELECT ON ag_catalog.ag_graph       EnsureGraph/DropGraph existence guard
  GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE <db>             create_graph builds a schema
EVERY pool in the package -- the battery arm and all of TestAGESessionInit's
pools -- logs in as this role. The superuser connection exists only for
bootstrap DDL and is closed before anything under test opens.

=== MUTATION PROOFS (all run against real containers, -count=1) ===

Requirement 1, the canary discriminates. Mutated the EMITTER
(internal/codegen/age/render_graph.go canaryStmt) to
  SELECT 'true'::ag_catalog.agtype = 'true'::ag_catalog.agtype
and regenerated every AGE golden, i.e. the mutation is "the emitter shipped a
weaker canary", not a hand-edit of one file. Result: exit 1 in 5.65s, red on
exactly the two discrimination assertions and nothing else --
  .../the_shipped_canary  "An error is expected but got nil"      (property C)
  .../the shipped canary refuses a session a weaker probe admits
                          "An error is expected but got nil"      (property B)
Property (A) stayed GREEN under the mutation, which is the bead's point stated
as a test result: a coarse broken-deployment test cannot tell the two canaries
apart, so only B and C carry the requirement.

Requirement 2, the non-superuser arm. Two mutations, run as a pair:
  2a  removed GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE from ageAppGrants
      -> TestLiveSmoke/apache-age-pgx-v5 exit 1, both scenarios red with
         gqlc: ensure graph "gqlc_live_1" (the name bound at New):
         ERROR: permission denied for database postgres (SQLSTATE 42501)
      The arm genuinely runs on the limited role's privileges.
  2b  same grant still removed, arm's pool DSN switched to ageSuperuser
      -> exit 0, PASS in 4.686s.
2b is .6's recorded defect reproduced in miniature: a battery that connects as
postgres certifies green a deployment the application role cannot run at all.

=== NIGHTLY GATE FAILS RED (not merely "a check exists") ===
Seeded require.Equal(t, "Alice", name) -> "AliceBROKEN" in the shared battery
and ran the literal nightly command, `just test-codegen-live-age`:
  exit 1, --- FAIL: TestLiveSmoke/apache-age-pgx-v5/one_col_one_param_one
  expected: "AliceBROKEN"  actual: "Alice"

=== PARALLELISM AND ISOLATION ===
ageArm.parallelScenarios() reports true; scenario graph names come from an
atomic counter and appear in the logs as gqlc_live_1 / gqlc_live_2. Isolation
mutation-proven earlier: forcing the name to a constant reds the arm with
duplicate key value violates unique constraint "pg_namespace_nspname_index"
(SQLSTATE 23505).
=== DESIGN DECISIONS THE BEAD DID NOT DICTATE ===

1. Battery interface split into read and write halves. The AGE target does not
   emit :exec yet (that is .10), so it cannot serve mixed_read_write_batch.
   Rather than let the AGE arm silently skip write scenarios, `harness` now
   carries only the scalar surface and `writeHarness` extends it; the `arms`
   table records `writes: bool` and TestLiveSmoke asserts
   `arm.writes == (h implements writeHarness)`. An arm that gains or loses
   :exec emission fails the battery until both are updated, instead of
   dropping scenarios unremarked. .10 flips one bool.

2. one_col_one_param_one added to the shared scalar battery, and its manifest
   gained the neo4j-go-v6 target (it had v5 + age only). Without it the only
   shared :one/sentinel coverage came from mixed_read_write_batch, which AGE
   cannot serve. Golden subtree for v6 regenerated via the conformance
   -update path.

3. TestAGESessionInit boots its own apache/age container rather than sharing
   the battery arm's. It creates roles, creates databases and drops an
   operator out of an extension; none of that should be observable by the
   arm the scalar battery drives. Cost is one extra postgres container, which
   is negligible next to the neo4j pair, and all four boot concurrently
   (full suite, -count=1, real containers: 35.6s).

4. The AGE session-init contract lives in its own file rather than as an arm
   scenario. It is not backend-parametric -- there is no neo4j analogue of a
   pool-acquisition hook -- so putting it in the shared battery would have
   meant a scenario only one arm can run.

5. openAGEPool now takes the AfterConnect hook as a parameter. The
   discrimination proof needs two pools over one DSN differing only in their
   hook; parametrising the one helper beats a near-duplicate of it.

6. `refuses(ctx, pool)` releases a connection the pool unexpectedly hands out
   before returning nil. Found the hard way: the first mutation run took the
   full 10m test timeout and died in a goroutine dump, because a leaked
   acquired resource blocks pgxpool.Close in t.Cleanup. With the release, the
   same mutation reds in 5.65s with a legible assertion. A red that takes ten
   minutes to print is a red nobody reads.
=== TWO RECORDED FACTS IN THIS BEAD ARE WRONG (found by the implementer,
verified by the manager, 2026-08-01) ===

--- 1. "PR CI wall-time must be untouched -- the codegen_live tag boundary
already guarantees that." FALSE, and it was a live trap. ---

I verified this at master 1335fae. .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml carried

    on:
      pull_request:
      workflow_dispatch:
      schedule:

and its own header opens "PR-blocking merge gate", noting that gqlc-rvw
promoted it to blocking. The build tag keeps codegen_live out of the DEFAULT
build; it does not keep it out of PR CI, because that workflow passes
-tags codegen_live explicitly. So the guarantee this bead relies on does not
exist, and the obvious implementation -- add the AGE arm to
just test-codegen-live -- would have booted an apache/age container on every
PR, which is the exact outcome the bead forbids while believing itself immune.

RESOLUTION (implementer's, accepted): split the recipe by backend rather than
gating the workflow wholesale.
    test-codegen-live-neo4j = -run TestLiveSmoke -skip 'TestLiveSmoke/apache-age'
    test-codegen-live-age   = -run 'TestLiveSmoke|TestAGESessionInit' -skip 'TestLiveSmoke/neo4j'
Job `neo4j` keeps every trigger; job `apache-age` carries
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
I confirmed the only PR-time step change is
    - just test-codegen-live
    + just test-codegen-live-neo4j
and that the new age recipe appears solely in the gated job. He also verified
empirically that -skip does not execute the excluded subtest body, by observing
which images actually boot: neo4j half boots neo4j@sha256:362542 only (18.3s),
age half boots apache/age@sha256:4241e2 only (7.8s). That is the right proof --
a -skip that still ran the body would show the other image.

--- 2. This bead's own "HOW TO APPLY" for the SessionInit failure path is not
constructible as written. ---

It says to "build a pool whose AfterConnect runs SessionInit against a session
with ag_catalog deliberately off search_path". You cannot: SessionInit's first
statement unconditionally PREPENDS ag_catalog to the search_path, so the
premise cannot be set up through the shipped hook. And every failure reachable
that way (extension absent, role lacks USAGE) fails a WEAK canary and the
shipped canary identically -- so it would have demonstrated nothing about
discrimination, which was the entire point of the requirement.

The requirement itself stands and is discharged; only the recipe was wrong.
Decomposed into: (A) an acquisition-time refusal table (42501 no-USAGE role,
3F000 no-extension DB) asserting Connect succeeds, NewWithConfig succeeds,
Acquire FAILS wrapped in "gqlc: AGE operator canary", TotalConns()==0;
(B) an acquire-observable A/B on a database with ONLY
ag_catalog.+(agtype,agtype) dropped -- the weak-probe pool acquires, the
shipped pool fails 42883; (C) statement replay off the search_path with the
canary captured via a pgx.QueryTracer, plus a rejected-literal table; (D) a
fence that every AGE target's SessionInit issues identical statements.

Note (B) is the sharp one: dropping a single operator is what separates the two
canaries, and it is exactly what "extension absent" cannot do.

--- SMALLER CORRECTIONS TO .6's RECORD ---
.6's note that '1' = '1' fails "inside agtype_to_bool" is right; its SQLSTATE
is 22023 (cannot_cast_agtype_value, agtype.c:2744).

.6's transcript implies a bare `appuser` can run the canary. It cannot --
42501, permission denied for schema ag_catalog. AGE grants NOTHING to PUBLIC.
The minimum set for a generated client is USAGE ON SCHEMA ag_catalog,
SELECT ON ag_catalog.ag_graph, and CREATE ON DATABASE. This matters for the
non-superuser requirement: "non-superuser" is not a single role, it is a
specific grant set, and that set is now pinned by ageAppGrants.
Manager rulings on Linus round-1 observations (round-1 verdict: PASS).

Independent verification of the PASS, done before ruling: I re-ran the unit
and lint gates green, then re-injected the historical gqlc-35yu.6 defect
myself -- `LOAD 'age'` prepended to the emitted SessionInit of
one_col_one_param_one -- and drove the AGE live arm both ways.

  RED as gqlc_app: `gqlc: load age: ERROR: access to library "age" is not
  allowed (SQLSTATE 42501)`, failing both TestLiveSmoke/apache-age-pgx-v5
  scenarios at EnsureGraph and TestAGESessionInit at capture.

  GREEN with the identical mutation and the app role created LOGIN SUPERUSER,
  nothing else changed: ok 4.59s, both scenarios passing against real graphs
  gqlc_live_1 / gqlc_live_2.

So the arm's redness is attributable to the least-privilege role and to
nothing else. Requirement 2 is load-bearing. Worktree restored to 84b63de.

NB1 (+0.7s PR-time on an 18.4s job) -- DECLINED. Proportionate.

NB2 ("every AGE target prepares a session identically" iterates a
hand-maintained 2-element list) -- PROMOTED, as a naming defect. There are 12
AGE golden targets; the list names 2. The property the arm actually depends
on is narrower and is what the list checks: the two packages the arm binds
together issue the same statements, which is what lets one pool serve handles
generated into both. Fix the name and the comment to claim that, not a
universal. The exhaustive claim over all 12 belongs offline, not behind a
container -- filed separately.

AGENTS.md violation. The mechanism is worth keeping, the contrast is not:

neither half still runs and reports as skipped.

rationale is a PR-cost argument, and it still holds for
test-codegen-live-neo4j, which is the PR gate -- leave that one cached.
test-codegen-live-age is nightly and manual only and test-codegen-live is
wired to no CI job at all, so neither has a PR cost to protect. For those two
the cache buys nothing and can serve a nightly a PASS it did not run.
MERGED as 5dd3c0a (PR #660). Issue #625 closed; umbrella #633 verified still
open. Epic gqlc-35yu now 8/12.

Round-1 review PASS over 11 mutations; I verified it independently by
re-injecting the historical .6 defect myself, red as the least-privilege role
(SQLSTATE 42501) and green with the same role created SUPERUSER.

A BLOCKING defect got past both the implementer and round-1 review, and is
worth recording because the class is not code:

The workflow split replaced the single job id `live-smoke` with `neo4j` and
`apache-age`. GitHub derives a check context from the job id, and master's
branch protection required the context list ["lint","test","tidy","actionlint",
"govulncheck","live-smoke","codegen-fence"]. So the split silently deleted a
required context. PR #660 could never have satisfied branch protection, and had
it merged, master would have required a context no workflow produces --
blocking every subsequent pull request in the repo.

I caught it by diffing the reported check names against the live protection
API, not by reading the YAML, which looks entirely correct on its own. Fixed
in-PR by renaming the jobs `live-smoke` / `live-smoke-age`, so no shared
branch-protection state had to be mutated. Both jobs now carry a comment
recording why their id is load-bearing.

GENERAL LESSON for the remaining epic beads: a workflow job rename is an
interface change against branch protection. Any bead touching .github/workflows
job ids must diff the produced contexts against
`gh api repos/areqag/gqlc/branches/master/protection`. Reviewing the YAML in
isolation cannot catch this.

Round 2 focused on that blind spot returned PASS. Two further comment
overclaims were promoted from it and fixed: the justfile comment described
arm-level -skip subtraction as if it also governed top-level tests, which are
bounded by each recipe's -run allowlist; and live-smoke-age gained the
mirror-image warning that it skips on pull requests and GitHub counts a
skipped check as satisfying a required context.

SessionInit) and gqlc-0oau (P2: the AGE arm's only gate is a nightly with no
failure alerting, subject to GitHub's 60-day cron disablement).

title: codegen/age: scalar read path — :one/:many methods, param encoding, agtype scalar decode, error taxonomy
description:
First query-bearing AGE stage. Emits per-query :one/:many methods for scalar params + scalar columns: the cypher() invocation uses the parameter mechanism the spike selected (server-side binding — string interpolation of user args is banned), column lists emitted as the AS (v0 ag_catalog.agtype, ...) projection, and emitted agtype scalar decode helpers (bool/integer/float/numeric/string/null, driven by the spike text corpus) in models.go. Error taxonomy mirrors the neo4j impl: ErrNoRows when :one matches nothing, ErrMultipleResults on more than one — identity-matchable sentinels (errors.Is).

TDD: for each fixture enrolled for the AGE target, write the golden red first, then emit; decode helpers get direct unit tests against the spike corpus text before any golden lands.
acceptance_criteria: Applicable valid fixtures gain AGE golden subtrees and pass; goldens compile under the generic build gate; decode helpers unit-tested against captured agtype text including malformed input; ErrNoRows/ErrMultipleResults emitted and sentinel-matchable; no fmt.Sprintf or string concatenation of user params anywhere in emitted query text.
notes:
=== SPIKE gqlc-35yu.5 OUTCOME — DECISIONS THIS BEAD DEPENDS ON ===
Full evidence in gqlc-35yu.5 (818 lines, incl. the complete agtype text
corpus this bead's decode helpers should be TDD'd against).

PARAMETER MECHANISM (selected, with server-log proof of server-side binding):
direct cypher('<graph>', $$...$$, $1) over the pgx extended protocol.
age_prepare_cypher was REJECTED — it latches query text into the plan via
connection-global state at Parse time, which pgx statement caching schedules
unpredictably. String interpolation of user args remains banned unconditionally;
note pgx SimpleProtocol (the only interpolating mode) is the one mode AGE
rejects outright, so the unsafe path fails closed.

BINDING GOTCHA — params must be bound as a Go `string`. Both []byte and
map[string]any FAIL. agtype travels as TEXT format in both directions, and its
OID is DATABASE-SPECIFIC (16461 on the spike container) — do NOT hard-code it.

DECODE GOTCHAS the corpus exposes, each of which a naive parser gets wrong:
  - ::vertex / ::edge / ::path / ::numeric are VALUE-LEVEL annotations at
    ARBITRARY DEPTH, not merely trailing suffixes.
  - Map keys come back in jsonb order: LENGTH FIRST, then lexicographic.
    Goldens must expect this ordering, not insertion or plain lexicographic.
  - NaN and Infinity are valid agtype but are NOT valid JSON — a plain
    encoding/json decode path will break on them.
  - NULL properties are DROPPED entirely. A nullable field comes back as an
    ABSENT KEY, never as an explicit null. This directly shapes the nullable
    decode + error taxonomy in this bead.

SESSION PRECONDITION (see gqlc-35yu.6): ag_catalog must be on the session
search_path or every WHERE/operator query fails — SessionInit enforces this.

GUARDRAIL from gqlc-35yu.6 review: internal/codegen/age/types.go returns "any" from Temporal for every kind, because TypeMap.Temporal has no rejection channel (gqlc-9n6t). Harmless at C0 — no query methods are emitted — but .7 is where query methods first appear for AGE, so this becomes reachable HERE. Until gqlc-9n6t lands, do NOT enrol any fixture with a temporal projection for the apache-age-pgx-v5 target: it would generate a column typed 'any' that nothing can decode, and the golden would freeze that as correct. Scalar projections are unaffected.
=== TWO .6-ROUND-2 GUARDS THIS BEAD MUST REMOVE (recorded 2026-08-01) ===
.6 makes the AGE target CLI-UNREACHABLE on purpose: generate hard-errors on any
query (age.ErrUnsupportedQuery), because emitting a client that silently drops
the user's queries is worse than refusing. .7 is the bead that makes AGE
reachable, so .7 owns retiring both guards. Recorded here so they are not
discovered by a user instead.

GUARD 1 -- init wizard picker. internal/cli/init.go builds its driver picker
from config.DriverValues(). .6 filters apache-age-pgx-v5 OUT of that picker,
because until queries are served the entry is a guaranteed-to-fail choice. The
exclusion is deliberately explicit and named at the call site rather than a
silent slice trim, precisely so .7 finds it. DELETE THE FILTER in .7.

GUARD 2 -- the query rejection itself. rejectUnservedQueries runs before
emission in internal/codegen/age/generate.go. It does NOT simply disappear in
.7: it NARROWS. .7 serves SCALAR params + SCALAR columns only. Everything else
-- entity columns (.9), writes (.10), temporal (.11) -- must still be REJECTED,
not silently emitted. Rewrite the predicate to reject what .7 does not serve;
do not delete the mechanism. It is load-bearing through .11.

GUARD 3 (consequence) -- the driver-axis test. .6's review (B3) established that
registry/vocabulary parity proved nothing about coverage: a fake fourth backend
registered cleanly and only three string-level assertions in internal/config
noticed. TestRunDriverAxis is therefore DERIVED from config.DriverValues() with
a per-driver expectation. AGE's expectation in .6 is the rejection behaviour.
.7 must UPDATE that expectation to the scalar-read behaviour rather than
deleting the AGE row -- deleting it re-opens exactly the coverage hole B3 shut.
=== GUARD 1 REFINEMENT: DELETE THE ENTRY, NOT THE MECHANISM (2026-08-01) ===
Correcting the "GUARD 1 -- init wizard picker" note above. My original ruling
was to filter AGE out of the picker. That was incomplete and the implementation
found the hole before it shipped.

WHAT WENT WRONG WITH THE NAIVE FILTER: huh resolves a Select value that is
absent from its options to INDEX 0. So on an EDIT of a config already naming
apache-age-pgx-v5, withholding the value made the wizard silently rewrite the
driver to neo4j-go-v5 the moment the user accepted the default. Withholding a
STORED value destroys the user's data -- strictly worse than the dead menu
entry the filter existed to remove. Caught by TestInitEditVocabularyPrefill
failing for a real reason.

SHIPPED SHAPE: offerableDrivers(current config.Driver) withholds from the
FRESH-CHOICE vocabulary but ALWAYS RETAINS THE CURRENT VALUE. A fresh `init`
never sees AGE; an edit of a config that already names it preserves it. The
withheld set is the named var driversWithoutQueryEmission at the call site.

HOW .7 APPLIES THIS: remove apache-age-pgx-v5 from driversWithoutQueryEmission.
DO NOT remove offerableDrivers or the retention behaviour. The list going empty
is the correct end state for this epic; the mechanism generalises to any future
backend that is registered before it can serve queries, and the prefill trap it
guards is a property of huh, not of AGE. Deleting the mechanism re-arms a bug
that silently rewrites user config.
=== INHERITED DEFECT from .6 (B2, found in .6 review round 3): the 63-BYTE name cast. This bead adds a THIRD site. ===

.6 binds the graph name through PostgreSQL's `name` type in two statements:
    EnsureGraph:  ag_catalog.create_graph($1::name)
    DropGraph:    ag_catalog.drop_graph($1::name, true)
`name` is NAMEDATALEN-1 = 63 BYTES, and the cast TRUNCATES SILENTLY -- no
error, no warning, no notice. Consequences proved against the pinned image:
two distinct names sharing a 63-byte prefix collapse to ONE graph; the second
EnsureGraph returns nil having created nothing; DropGraph on the second
CASCADE-DROPS the first's graph, its labels and its data.

.6 fixes it by REJECTING len(graph) > 63 (Go len, i.e. BYTES) inside
EnsureGraph and DropGraph -- not in New, which stays I/O-free, error-free and
panic-free, matching the neo4j constructor. See the ruling on .6.

WHY IT LANDS HERE: this bead passes the bound graph name into
    ag_catalog.cypher($1, $$ ... $$) AS (...)
which is a third site where a truncated name silently addresses the WRONG
GRAPH -- and the worst-behaved of the three, because it is on the READ path.
A query against a 68-byte name would return another graph's rows as if they
were its own. EnsureGraph/DropGraph at least fail loudly once .6 lands; a
read that silently answers from a neighbouring graph does not.

WHAT TO DO HERE: do NOT add a fourth ad-hoc length check at the cypher() call
site. The guard belongs at ONE choke point that every graph-name-binding
statement passes through, and .7 is the bead where the second consumer appears
and the choke point becomes worth having. Factor .6's check into that shared
guard and route cypher() through it. Test the boundary in BYTES, not
characters -- a 63-character multibyte name is over the limit and a
rune-counting test will not see it (see .6's note on the two length axes).

=== RE-ENROLMENT OWED HERE (from .6 round 4, 2026-08-01) ===
.6 removed apache-age-pgx-v5 from the targets of
test/data/codegen/invalid/identifier_collision_graph_lifecycle.

Why it had to go: .6 reordered generate() so rejectUnservedQueries runs BEFORE
codegen.Prepare, so AGE returns ErrUnsupportedQuery before Prepare can reach
ErrIdentifierCollision, and a manifest carries ONE expectedError for all its
targets. At C0 the enrolment was never exercising the path it names -- AGE
rejects any query outright, and a query-free batch has no names to collide.

.7 IS WHERE IT BECOMES REACHABLE: scalar queries are servable here, so a query
named EnsureGraph or DropGraph survives rejectUnservedQueries and reaches
Prepare's Phase A for real. PUT apache-age-pgx-v5 BACK in that manifest's
targets and confirm it goes red for the right reason -- ErrIdentifierCollision,
not ErrUnsupportedQuery.

Harness constraint to know before starting: sentinelByName in
internal/codegen/conformance/conformance_test.go is built only from
codegenSentinels and queryfile.AllSentinels(). Backend-package sentinels like
age.ErrUnsupportedQuery are NOT registrable as a manifest expectedError without
a harness change. If .7's narrowed rejection needs fixture coverage of its own,
that harness change is part of this bead.

The reserved set itself is uniform across backends and stays fenced throughout
by TestReservedIdentifiersAreUniformAcrossBackends (internal/codegen/prepare_test.go:342).
=== HAZARD THAT DIES WITH GUARD 1 (from .6 round-4 review, 2026-08-01) ===
internal/cli/init.go:206-209 does:
    offerable := offerableDrivers(noCurrentDriver)
    ... offerable[0]
That index is unguarded. It is safe today only because driversWithoutQueryEmission
is a strict subset of config.DriverValues(), so the filter can never empty the
slice. A future stage that withheld EVERY driver would panic in the init wizard.

I declined to add a fence in .6 because .7 DELETES the filter (guard 1 in the
note above), which removes offerableDrivers and the index with it. A fence for
code with a scheduled deletion date is churn.

SO: when you delete guard 1, confirm the deletion actually takes the unguarded
index with it. If any part of offerableDrivers survives — e.g. the picker keeps
a derived slice for some other reason — then the hazard survives too and needs
either a non-empty invariant test or a guard at that point. Do not leave the
filter half-removed.
=== CORRECTION to the inherited-B2 note above (manager, verified live 2026-08-01) ===

The mechanism I recorded above is WRONG. The note says this bead "passes the
bound graph name into ag_catalog.cypher($1, ...)". It cannot. Carmack found
this while implementing; I reproduced it against the pinned image
(apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86...feb70eb) before accepting it.

AGE resolves cypher()'s FIRST argument at parse analysis, and accepts a
literal constant there and nothing else. All of these fail identically with
ERROR: a name constant is expected:
    PREPARE q(name) AS SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher($1, $$ ... $$) ...
    PREPARE q(text) AS SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher($1, $$ ... $$) ...
    PREPARE q      AS SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher($1, $$ ... $$) ...
    SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher(repeat(E'a',1), $$ ... $$) ...
The last one matters: it is not merely that BIND parameters are refused, it is
that no runtime-evaluated expression is accepted at all. Splicing the name into
the statement text is the ONLY mechanism available, not a chosen one.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION: the conclusion, entirely. cypher() IS a third
name-binding site, it IS the worst-behaved of the three because it is on the
read path, and the guard DOES belong at one shared choke point. Confirmed live:
  - create_graph(repeat('a',70)) SUCCEEDS and stores 63 octets. NOTICE only,
    no error, no warning.
  - a'70 and a'63||'XXXXXXX' are distinct names that collapse to ONE graph --
    the second create_graph reports "already exists". This is exactly the
    "could address another graph" hazard boundGraph's error message names.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GUARD'S PLACEMENT: because the name is composed into text
rather than bound, the length check must run BEFORE composition, not at the
call site. It sits at boundGraph() in render_db.go, the only reader of q.graph;
EnsureGraph, DropGraph and cypherStmt all source the name from it.

ON THE INTERPOLATION BAN: I told the implementer that string interpolation of
user args is banned unconditionally. That ban is intact. Query ARGUMENTS still
bind -- they travel as a third ag_catalog.agtype parameter, $1, verified:
  PREPARE qargs(agtype) AS SELECT * FROM ag_catalog.cypher(E'g',
    $$ MATCH (n) WHERE n.k = $k RETURN n.k $$, $1) AS t(k agtype);
  EXECUTE qargs('{"k": 42}');  -- returns 42
Only the graph name is spliced, escaped as an E-string (backslash then quote).
I verified the escape contains a break-out attempt: a name payload of
    x', $q$ $q$) AS (n agtype); DROP TABLE victim; --
emitted through that escaping parsed as ONE string literal and the DROP never
ran (victim survived). Separately, AGE independently rejects graph names
containing ' or \ with "graph name is invalid" at create_graph -- so the escape
is defence in depth at the SQL layer, not the only thing standing there.
=== REVIEW ROUND 1 (Linus) — FAIL. Manager rulings, 2026-08-01 ===

WHAT HELD, so a later round does not re-litigate it. The reviewer mutated all
four agtype decode helpers and the ErrNoRows path, ran conformance with
-update, and every fence stayed red -- the compiled-corpus harness extracts
models.go into a throwaway module and runs it, so -update cannot reach it.
Mutating len(q.graph) to len([]rune(q.graph)) went red on both the AST fence
and the multibyte corpus rows. He also established live that an absent property
and a literal RETURN null both come back as SQL NULL, not the 4-byte text
"null", so writeScan's raw == nil discriminator rests on the right model.

TEMPORAL: no finding, and the earlier worry is answered. typeMap.Temporal is
UNREACHABLE from generate() -- unservedColumn (errors.go:88) rejects
ResolvedTemporal before Prepare, and scalarWidth rejects the five temporal
widths via typeMap.Property. Both have positive tests. Not enrolling a temporal
fixture was correct and the absence is fenced, not merely observed. This
supersedes the concern that fed gqlc-9n6t for the AGE side of that bead.

--- B1, BLOCKING, verified by me before relaying ---
dollarTag (render_queries.go:46) guards with !strings.Contains(text, tag), but
what reaches the parser is tag+text+tag, so the tag can STRADDLE the text/tag
boundary while being absent from text alone. Text ending in $gqlc composes to
...$gqlc$gqlc$ and PostgreSQL closes at the straddle.

Reproduced by me against the pinned image:
    SELECT $gqlc$MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name
    // trailing $gqlc$gqlc$ AS should_fail;
    ERROR:  syntax error at or near "AS"
and strpos(E'...// trailing $gqlc', '$gqlc$') = 0 confirms the Go-side guard
passes the tag through. Control case with no $gqlc closes correctly.

Generated code that cannot run, emitted with no diagnostic, and dollarTag's own
doc comment asserts exactly the property it lacks. Reachable today via a
trailing comment; ordinary at .10, where SET p.name = $gqlc ends a write query
in a property-typed parameter. Ruled: strings.Index(text+tag, tag) == len(text)
-- subsumes the old check rather than sitting beside it. The i > 0 escalation
branch has never executed in the suite and must be covered.

--- N1, PROMOTED to required ---
The E-string escaping in cypherStmt (render_db.go:114) is fenced ONLY by a
golden: deleting the ReplaceAll pair and running -update leaves test, lint and
fence all green. Filed non-blocking because the behaviour is correct. I
promoted it because I verified the escaping is load-bearing -- an injection
payload emitted through it arrives as one literal and the DROP does not run --
and a security-relevant splice fenced by an artefact -update rewrites is the
exact laundering class this suite is otherwise built to defeat. Fix is one
line: add cypherStmt to the declarations(...) call at corpus_test.go:49, which
already compiles boundGraph. B1's tag choice goes in the same fence.

--- N2, PROMOTED to required. The .6 conditional fired. ---
.6's note said: if any part of offerableDrivers survives guard 1's deletion,
the unguarded offerable[0] at internal/cli/init.go:206 survives too and needs a
non-empty invariant test or a guard. driversWithoutQueryEmission was EMPTIED
rather than removed -- correct, the retention behaviour stays useful for later
stages -- so the index survives and the conditional fires. Existing coverage
does not close it: init_test.go:825 passes the CURRENT driver, which the
d != current condition always retains, so that call can never return empty.
Line 206 passes noCurrentDriver, which can. One require.NotEmpty on
offerableDrivers(noCurrentDriver) closes it.

--- N3, DECLINED ---
Narrow-width overflow (int8(value0) for 300, float32 for 1e300) is silent, but
neo4j/render_queries.go:493-499 established carrier-then-convert as the
epic-wide convention, matching sqlc. Raised only so it is not mistaken for an
AGE-specific gap. Not this bead's to change; if revisited it is an epic-wide
decision. No bead filed.
=== REVIEW ROUND 2 (fresh Linus) — PASS, verified by the manager. 2026-08-01 ===

All three required fixes landed in ba6cd23..4db6bdb (4fb05db B1, c6fdfc7 N1,
4db6bdb N2). PR #657.

WHAT THE REVIEWER ESTABLISHED that is worth keeping, because it is reasoning
about the SERVER, not about our code, and the next backend bead will want it:

B1's predicate is correct for the right reason, not just for the reported
example. PostgreSQL's scan.l consumes the opening tag as one token, so the
dollar-quote scan begins at index 0 of text+tag; when a different dollar
delimiter matches inside the body the lexer does yyless(1), advancing exactly
one byte, so it can never skip a candidate start. The literal therefore closes
at the FIRST occurrence at or after that point, which is exactly what
strings.Index(text+tag, tag) == len(text) names. Occurrences straddling the
OPENING tag are correctly out of scope because that region is already tokenised.
Termination: rejection needs an occurrence starting at some j < len(text), and
two candidates cannot both match at one j (they diverge at byte 5), so the loop
ends within len(text)+1 turns.

He also checked whether the straddle class exists ELSEWHERE rather than assuming
dollarTag was the only site, and found the one other raw composition --
render_queries.go:89 emitting SourceText into a Go raw string, where the grammar
does admit backtick-escaped identifiers. Already closed upstream:
prepare.go:571 rejects any query whose source text holds a backtick with
ErrOutOfC6Scope, confirmed live. Every other user-controlled value reaching
emitted source goes through %q or is a validated Go identifier. Only the graph
name is spliced raw, which is N1's subject.

MANAGER'S INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION, not taken from the report:
- All four gates re-run by me. test/lint/fence green; live at 18.068s with
  -count=1 after `just test-codegen-live` first handed me a CACHED ok -- the
  trap fired on me, noting it so the next bead does not trust a bare recipe run.
- I re-ran the N1 laundering attack myself, since I was the one who promoted it
  to blocking. Replaced the escaping with a no-op ReplaceAll (keeping `strings`
  used so the failure is behavioural, not a compile error). The corpus fence
  went red naming my injection payload; I then ran conformance -count=1 -update,
  which rewrote all 11 AGE db.go goldens and reported ok -- i.e. the laundering
  reproduced -- and the fence STAYED RED. That is the property the promotion
  demanded. Worktree restored to 4db6bdb clean afterwards.
- I verified the 11-golden reflow from c6fdfc7 is comment-only: every changed
  line in those files is a comment or blank, no code churn.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: gqlc-7f9a (P3). Go raw string literals discard \r, so the
emitted query constant can differ from the bytes dollarTag was computed on --
the same invariant as B1 failing for a different reason. Epic-wide (age and
neo4j emit byte-identically) and reachable only via a bare \r inside the token,
so not held against this bead. There is no CRLF normalisation in
internal/queryfile; I checked.

DECLINED AGAIN at round 2: the reviewer re-raised narrow-width overflow as
epic-wide context only, and noted graphStub's hardcoded import list in
corpus_test.go:29 is a future confusing-compile-error risk rather than a gap.
Neither blocks; neither gets a bead.
